subject: Urgent: Eval-flagged regression and release exception request
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval flagged regression in billing_summary prompt set — request hold

Team,

Our nightly evals flagged a regression in the billing_summary prompt set for model r2.3. The automated suite shows a ~3.6% drop in entity-F1 (billing amounts and dates) vs. the baseline and several hallucination cases in the top 50 samples. I attached the eval-report.pdf with the failing samples and diffs.

Impact: Optima Health (large customer) surfacing incorrect invoice totals in the example flows. They flagged this in a support thread this morning and asked if the new release is responsible.

Ask: Can we hold the r2.3 release until we confirm whether this is a true model regression vs. a dataset artifact? If we keep the release, we should plan an immediate canary + rollback window for Optima.

Questions I need answered by EOD:
- Can infra/serving reproduce on the production prompt set (fixed temperature, 1-shot seeds)?
- Is there an easy mitigation (decoding tweak / prompt tweak) we can ship in the patch?
- Suggested acceptance criteria for release continuation (numeric).

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Evals & Quality
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval-report.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval flagged regression in billing_summary prompt set — request hold

Laura — thanks for the heads-up and for the detailed report. I pulled a few of the failing examples and tried to reproduce locally against the same r2.3 binary (cpu/gpu parity verified). I can reproduce the entity-F1 drop on the canonical prompt set when sampling temperature is 0.8; with deterministic decoding (greedy) the regression shrinks considerably.

Proposal (short):
- Immediate triage: engineering runs a targeted eval with production prompt temperature and top-k parameters (Neha, can you run this by EOD?)
- If we can mitigate by changing default decoding config for billing_summary (e.g., reduce temp to 0.6 + top_p 0.9), we can ship a minor config patch and run a canary.
- If not, we put r2.3 on hold and plan an A/B rollback for Optima.

Acceptance criteria suggestion:
- Entity-F1 delta <= 0.5% vs baseline on the canonical prompt set (primary metric)
- Hallucination rate (as per eval rubric) not exceeding baseline + 0.2%
- No customer-facing error-class > 0.8% during 24h canary

I added Evelyn to help with the risk decision if we need an exception to the release calendar (since Optima is a strategic account). Link to triage doc: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/optima-eval-2026-06

—Jonas
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime

Adding context from CS: Optima hit the issue in a staged rollout and paused the feature on their side — they're seeing 2 examples that materially affect downstream reconciliation in their demo flows. Olivia is copied.

My recommended next steps (owner tags):
1) Neha — run targeted production-config eval (temp/top_p) + reproduce with the full Optima prompt set. Please attach the eval logs and a small reproducible prompt set. (ETA: 6/4 EOD)
2) Jonas/Infra — prepare a 5% canary plan that routes Optima traffic to a rollback-capable variant. Include monitoring thresholds and an automated rollback hook. (ETA: 6/7)
3) Laura/Product — prepare customer comms + acceptance checklist we can run during canary. (ETA: 6/6)
4) Marissa/CS — coordinate Optima's availability for a 24h canary (they requested mornings PST). (ETA: 6/5)

I put together an initial A/B plan (ab_plan.md) attached — it includes traffic split, metrics to watch, and a two-tier rollback policy. If infra can change default decoding parameters quickly, that is the lowest-risk path; otherwise we do canary + rollback.

Olivia — can you confirm whether Optima is OK with a 5% canary next week and whether they want a pre-approved rollback window?

Thanks,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager

Attachments: ab_plan.md

Thanks for the quick triage and the invite. Optima can do a 5% canary starting Tue morning (PST). Two asks from our side:
- Please confirm the rollback window and how quickly you can switch traffic back (we need a max 30 min rollback SLA for this flow).
- Can you provide a short list of sample-rejection criteria we can surface to our product owners during the canary? (I want to avoid false positives in our monitoring.)

We also appreciate a short post-canary summary we can include in our internal QA notes.

Optima Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Quick summary and agreed plan: (finalized after sync)
- Run a 5% canary for Optima beginning Tue 2026-06-15 08:00 PST for 24 hours.
- Acceptance criteria (pass = safe to continue roll):
  * Entity-F1 delta <= 0.5% vs baseline on canonical + Optima prompt sets
  * Hallucination rate <= baseline + 0.2%
  * Customer-visible error-class (incorrect totals) < 0.8% during canary
- If any of the above fail, infra executes automated rollback (target: < 30 minutes) and we halt the release.
- Owners: Neha runs the reproduction evals and produces logs + diff.patch; Jonas/infra owns canary routing and rollback; Laura owns customer comms; Marissa owns Optima coord.
- Deliverables before canary: reproducible prompt set + logs (Neha), ab_plan.md updated with monitoring thresholds (Marissa), canary runbook + rollback playbook (Jonas).

I attached a small debug diff (diff.patch) with instrumentation hooks we used during repro. I'll upload the detailed logs to the shared drive and link SUP-3129 for tracking.

If we hit the rollback we will schedule a post-mortem within 48 hours.

Neha Kapoor
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
